alerts.observedDataflow: The expanded authenticated UI shows 58 steps starting at deploy/provider_gateway.py:48 value[gatewayOAuth], following redirectPort/redirect_port through provider.py:180 and TOML serialization to install_recovery.py:325,171,172.
sourceEvidence: deploy/provider_gateway.py:27-36 permits only public OAuth policy fields; redirectPort is constrained to integer 1024..65535. URL validation rejects embedded username/password.
deploy/provider_gateway.py:48-53 emits public endpoint/client/cookie-name/redirect-port policy; it does not emit native OAuth token values.
deploy/provider.py:177-180 serializes that public definition into TOML.
deploy/install_recovery.py:317 fixes initial settings to kind chatgpt, so the chatgpt-gateway branch from the reported path is not entered by this initialization call.
sinkEvidence: CreationPlan.file at lines171-173 records content SHA256 alongside kind/mode/uid/gid as the file identity; content remains separately tracked.
CreationPlan.bind at lines185-191 checks equality with the retained private creation plan during recovery.
private_record at lines22-28 enforces a root-owned mode0600 regular file; publish/verify also enforce claimed file identity, permissions and exact content.
passwordBoundary: deploy/accounts.py:44-50 uses a fresh 32-byte salt and scrypt N32768,r8,p3,dklen64; the returned bootstrap contains salt/hash/parameters, not plaintext password.
deploy/install_recovery.py:332 serializes that already-scrypt-derived bootstrap record.
alerts.conclusion: This SHA256 is not the account password verifier. The actual alert source is public configuration, and the sink is a recovery integrity digest. No password-hashing change is warranted for this alert.

sourceEvidence: tests/deploy/test_https_health.py:152 binds the synthetic server only to loopback127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port.
Lines153-156 create SSLContext(PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER), load disposable test certificates and wrap the loopback socket; no protocol downgrade is configured.
The CI workflow pins Python3.12.10. Official Python3.12 documentation states PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER uses TLS1.2 as minimum since Python3.10.
deploy/https_health.py:141-145 additionally sets minimum_version=TLSv1_2, check_hostname=True, hostname_checks_common_name=False and CERT_REQUIRED for the actual health probe.
tests/deploy/test_https_health.py:89,125-127 use a synthetic proof key; lines193-194 assert no Authorization or Cookie header.

officialReference.fact: PROTOCOL_TLS, PROTOCOL_TLS_CLIENT and PROTOCOL_TLS_SERVER have a minimum of TLS1.2.

alerts.conclusion: The alert assumes older permissive defaults; supported Python and the production client do not permit TLS1.0/1.1 here. This is a test fixture, not a production TLS listener. No source change is required to resolve a demonstrated security defect.

sourceEvidence: tests/deploy/test_dns_tls.py:26-34 creates TemporaryDirectory, registers cleanup, constructs an input JSON from explicit isolated-fake-access-id and isolated-fake-access-secret literals, writes it and applies mode0600.
No user credential, account data or protected environment value feeds this fixture.
The parser tests exercise private-file ownership/mode, malformed fields, redaction and selected-provider environment behavior.
deploy/dns_tls.py:23-35 enforces an absolute non-symlink bounded single-link root-owned mode0600 credential input in production; immutable managed credential directories are mode0700 and files0600.
alerts.conclusion: The flagged write stores only disposable synthetic input needed to exercise the credential-file parser, not real secret material.
